key_decisions.ma_choice: NUM_BTN parameter, default 4, with replicated independent channels via a generate loop
key_decisions.plan_choice: NUM_BUTTONS parameter, default 4, with identical independent channels

key_decisions.ma_choice: CLK_HZ plus DEBOUNCE_MS (milliseconds); CNT_MAX and CNT_W derived as localparams
key_decisions.plan_choice: CLK_FREQ_HZ plus DEBOUNCE_US (microseconds, default 10000); count and width derived
key_decisions.note: The spec requires a build-time setting and no hard-coded clock, but leaves the unit open. Microseconds give finer tuning; the structure is unchanged.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Divide CLK_HZ/1000 first to avoid 32-bit overflow; $error if the count rounds to 0
key_decisions.plan_choice: Order the division or use 64-bit math; elaboration checks or $error for a count of 0 or 1 and for counts that are too large

key_decisions.ma_choice: SYNC_STAGES parameter, default 2 (range 2-4), ASYNC_REG/don't-touch attributes, one synchronizer per bit
key_decisions.plan_choice: SYNC_STAGES parameter, default 2 and minimum 2, ASYNC_REG/keep attributes, plus a false-path constraint note
key_decisions.note: The spec requires a synchronizer but not its depth.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Invert before the first sync flop, so the synchronizer resets to 0
key_decisions.plan_choice: Invert after the last sync stage; no logic before the first flop; synchronizer resets to the raw idle value 1
key_decisions.note: Both keep the internal logic active-high. The only effect is on the synchronizer reset value.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Counter increments while the synced input differs from level_q and clears on any agreement; level flips after CNT_MAX+1 consecutive cycles; the rule is symmetric for press and release
key_decisions.plan_choice: Continuous stable-window counter that holds at 0 on match, increments on mismatch, and flips the state at the terminal count

key_decisions.ma_choice: Independent full-width counter per channel, with no shared prescaler
key_decisions.plan_choice: Independent full-width counter per button counting clock cycles

key_decisions.ma_choice: level_d1_q delayed copy; rise and fall decoded combinationally from level_q and level_d1_q; the pulse coincides with the first cycle of the new level
key_decisions.plan_choice: Dedicated pulse registers set on the same edge that flips level (flip & ~state / flip & state); all outputs come directly from flops
key_decisions.note: The pulse timing relative to the level is the same. The plan registers the pulses, while the MA decodes them from two flops. Both are glitch-free.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Active-low reset, asynchronous assert and synchronous de-assert supplied by the reset controller; no internal reset synchronizer
key_decisions.plan_choice: Asynchronous active-low reset on all flops; de-assertion assumed synchronized externally

key_decisions.decision: Power-up state and button held through reset
key_decisions.ma_choice: All registers reset to released/0; a held button produces one rise pulse after the debounce time
key_decisions.plan_choice: Levels reset to 0 (released); a held button is reported as a normal press with a pulse after one debounce time

key_decisions.ma_choice: Pulses are 1 clk wide and sampled in the same domain; no sticky or W1C event bits (noted as a future option)
key_decisions.plan_choice: No interrupt or bus interface; outputs consumed in the same clk domain (stated as an assumption)

key_decisions.ma_choice: Three NUM_BTN-wide vectors: level, rise, fall
key_decisions.plan_choice: Three NUM_BUTTONS-wide vectors: level, press pulse, release pulse

key_decisions.ma_choice: Bounce model, scaled-down parameters plus one real-parameter run, boundary glitch tests at CNT_MAX and CNT_MAX+1, SVA for pulse width, exclusivity and alternation
key_decisions.plan_choice: Randomized bounce generator, scaled debounce time plus a real-parameter run, scoreboard, and assertions for pulse width, exclusivity and N stable cycles; parameter sweeps; CDC lint
key_decisions.note: The plan does not explicitly list the exact CNT_MAX boundary glitch test, but it is otherwise aligned.

summary: The plan agrees closely with the MA. It matches on the parameterized channel count, derived terminal count with overflow and $error handling, a 2-stage parameterizable synchronizer with ASYNC_REG, the restart-on-change stability counter, per-channel counters, the reset style, power-up behaviour with a held button, the three output vectors, the same-domain consumer assumption and the verification approach. There are three differences, all equivalent: the debounce unit (microseconds vs milliseconds), inversion after rather than before the synchronizer, and registered pulse flops instead of a delayed-copy combinational decode, with the same visible timing. No questions were asked, so none were needless.
